observations: eps = 1e-10 is a sound pick under the brief: of the four candidates, 3e-10 fails (68 % of the forward stars at 0.999c; 16 % and +3.7 EV at 0.9999c), 1e-10 keeps 84 % at 0.999c with no eye shift and 28 % at 0.9999c with the starbow cluster plainly readable and blue in the cells I opened; the Doppler colours and the CMB disc stay readable. At the cap no catalogue star is visible with or without the glow (eye at EV +12.5 on the CMB disc), so 'every speed' can only mean up to 0.9999c for any eps.

Colour: 0.99c (1358 K) invisible, 0.999c (2482 K) a faint orange-brown veil, 0.9999c (4449 K) a warm grey-brown wash, cap (14114 K) a navy blue-white sky in the interior with the orange CMB dot; capture frames 10_b099_glow and 13_cap_glow carry the sim's pole and temperature.

'Visible from gamma 13.5' is the model criterion (0.3 x dark sky, HB-112); in the renders the 0.999c cell (6 dark skies) is only a faint veil and the cue is clearly readable from ~0.9999c; the sheet has no cell between gamma 10 and gamma 22.

The Crumey point-threshold fit changes branch at 0.0708 cd/m^2, so lim_pole is non-monotonic between ~550 and ~1,700 dark skies (4.78 at 546, 5.05 at 1,640); pre-existing package/mirror behaviour, affects only the 0.9999c row's threshold.
The sheet's absolute star counts depend on the catalogue build; record the catalogue sha in glow_eps_sheet.json.
Package drift note for #7: the PR body's own note is accurate.
